measurements.verbatim_quote: To assess the in vitro effects of ARC187 on heparin and protamine functions, blood from 3 individuals was drawn into 4-5 units/mL heparin, doses associated with heparin levels used in CABG surgery. The coagulability of these samples was assessed using the activated clot time (ACT), a whole blood coagulation test routinely used to monitor heparin activity during surgery. At these concentrations of heparin, in the absence of other additives, the ACT was significantly prolonged from a baseline value of ˜150 seconds to ˜500 seconds in the presence of 4 U/mL heparin or ˜800 seconds in the presence of 5 U/mL heparin. Addition of 10 μM ARC187 to these samples had little effect on clot time, demonstrating that ARC187 does not interfere with the anticoagulant activity of heparin.

--- VERBATIM QUOTE CONVENTION ---
Quotes are copied byte-for-byte from the HTML-to-text conversions in /home/user/coag-staging/fulltext, including the
sources' own typographic quirks: the tilde-like character in "~150 seconds" is U+02DC (MODIFIER LETTER SMALL TILDE) as
the converter emitted it, micro sign is the Greek mu in some places and an ASCII "uM" in others WITHIN THE SAME
PARAGRAPH of US 7,538,211 (Example 6B mixes "20 μM" and "10 uM"), and Table 9 of US 8,389,488 prints "hFV7a" where
"hFVIIa" is meant. None of these were silently normalised.

--- CO-ADMINISTERED AGENTS (schema gap) ---
The output schema has no field for a co-administered agent, but S32 is a reversal/rescue dataset in which the readout
belongs to a compound PAIR, and S61's heparin/protamine work is drug-drug interaction data. Collapsing those rows onto a
single compound would be wrong. Convention used: every affected measurement row's `notes` BEGINS with the machine-
parseable key `co_administered_agent=<agent>` (and, where stated, `co_administered_dose=<dose>`), with
`co_administered_agent=none` written explicitly on the matched single-agent arms so the pair structure is recoverable by
a downstream parser. 24 rows carry this key (18 in S32, 6 in S61). A reviewer promoting these to real columns should key on that prefix.

--- S5, US 5,886,165 (Hybridon) : the rarest data shape in the bundle ---
Table 1 gives, PER OLIGO, the concentration producing 50% aPTT prolongation - an EC50-style potency per compound rather
than one dose-response curve. All eight compounds share one 25-mer sequence and one experiment, so the differences are
attributable to backbone chemistry alone. The all-PS 3'-5' control (SEQ ID NO 8) is by far the most potent at 23.2
ug/mL; the three all-phosphodiester compounds (SEQ ID NOs 1, 4, 7) never reach 50% prolongation up to 100 ug/mL.

  PARSING HAZARD 1 (would silently corrupt the table): in the text conversion, seven of the eight rows WRAP onto a
  second line immediately before the aPTT value. Row 4 is the only single-line row. A line-based parse therefore reads
  the wrong column for 7/8 rows. The correct column order is: SEQ ID NO | Tm(DNA) | Tm(RNA) | HIV-1 IC50 (nM) |
  lymphocyte proliferation stimulation index at 10 ug/ml | 50% prolongation of clotting aPTT (ug/ml) | 50% inhibition of
  complement lysis (ug/ml). The aPTT value is the SIXTH field.

  PARSING HAZARD 2: ">>100.0" is a double greater-than, not a typo for ">100.0" and emphatically not 100. Encoded as
  readout_value ">100" with notes 'right_censored', per bundle instruction. Corroborated by Example 9's prose
  ("negligible effect up to 100 μg/ml dose"). Note also that the complement column of the same table uses a SINGLE
  ">500.0" - the source distinguishes the two censoring notations, so do not normalise them together.

  CONTRADICTION FOUND (source-internal). Example 9 states: "In the case of phosphorothioate-MBOs, a 2-3.5 fold higher
  concentration dose was required to attain the same extent of clotting prolongation compared to that of oligonucleotide
  SEQ ID NO 8." The printed table does not support "2-3.5 fold" for all four PS-MBOs. Against SEQ ID NO 8 at 23.2 ug/mL:
  SEQ 2 = 51.1 (2.2x), SEQ 3 = 58.0 (2.5x), SEQ 6 = 98.3 (4.2x), SEQ 5 = 115.0 (5.0x). Two of the four exceed the stated
  range. The TABLE values are extracted; the prose range is not. A reviewer should treat "2-3.5 fold" as the source's own
  error and prefer the table.

  SEQUENCE CAVEAT. The SEQUENCE LISTING prints all eight as 25-mers of the same base sequence, with U/T being the only
  difference between MBOs and controls (e.g. SEQ ID NO 1 = CUCTCGCACCCATCTCTCTCCUUCT vs SEQ ID NO 7 =
  CTCTCGCACCCATCTCTCTCCTTCT). That U/T pattern does NOT fully mark the ribonucleotide positions: SEQ ID NO 1 differs
  from the all-DNA control at only three positions (2, 22, 23), while Example 1 states there are "three 2'-5'-linkages at
  each of the 5'- and 3'-ends"; position 25 is still printed T. SEQ ID NOs 1, 2 and 3 are printed identically, as are 4,
  5 and 6, even though they differ in phosphorothioate content. The actual per-position layout is drawn only in FIG. 1
  (white rectangles = phosphodiester segments, black = phosphorothioate), which is an image and was not read. This is why
  no `modifications` rows exist for the S5 compounds - modelling them from the U/T pattern would be fabrication.
  `sequence_base` for the S5 oligos is the printed listing with U mechanically normalised to T; this is flagged in each
  oligo's notes.

--- S32, US 8,389,488 (Isis) : the only reversal/rescue dataset ---
Table 8 ("Effect of antidote treatment on aPTT INR") is the numeric core: aPTT INR at six timepoints for ISIS 404071
(Factor XI ASO) alone and with its complementary antidote ISIS 418026, extracted as 12 rows. Table 9 supplies a
thrombotic outcome (FeCl3 vena cava model) rescued by a NON-oligonucleotide antidote, human Factor VIIa protein.

  These are ON-TARGET pharmacology rows, not toxicity: the compounds are designed anticoagulants. on_target_effect=true
  and unintended_toxicity=false throughout S32.

  Table 8 has NO PBS-only (no-antisense) row, so the control for the combination arm is the antisense-only arm, and the
  absolute baseline is not printed - control_value is NOT_REPORTED for the antisense-alone rows.

  DOSE INCONSISTENCY ACROSS EXAMPLES (easy to conflate): the Table 8 aPTT experiment used ISIS 404071 at 40 mg/kg twice
  weekly (Example 15); the Table 9 thrombosis experiment used 20 mg/kg twice weekly (Example 16); the prothrombin
  experiment (Examples 8-12) used ISIS 401025 at 30 mg/kg. Each row carries its own dose.

  PLATELET CAVEAT ON TABLE 9. The measured analyte is platelet factor-4 quantified by real-time PCR. It is extracted here
  because the source uses it purely as a surrogate for THROMBUS MASS in an FeCl3 venous thrombosis model driven by Factor
  XI knockdown - a coagulation-cascade outcome. It is NOT a platelet-count / thrombocytopenia readout and must not be
  routed to the thrombocytopenia dossier.

  SEQUENCE DEFECT IN THE SOURCE. Table 4 prints ISIS 401025 as ATTCCATAGTGTAGGCCTT - 19 nt, which cannot be a 5-10-5
  gapmer (20 nt). Its stated antidote ISIS 405277 (AAGGACCTACACTATGGAAT) reverse-complements to ATTCCATAGTGTAGGTCCTT,
  so the printed 401025 appears to be missing one T at position 16. Recorded exactly as printed and flagged; NOT
  corrected. By contrast ISIS 418026 was verified to be the exact reverse complement of ISIS 404071, so that pair is
  internally consistent.

  FIGURE-ONLY ENDPOINTS. Thrombin generation (Example 11 / FIG. 7), PT-INR (Example 12 / FIG. 8) and relative aPTT
  (Example 12 / FIG. 9) for the prothrombin antisense/antidote experiment were measured but the results exist ONLY as
  plotted panels. Three rows are recorded with readout_value NOT_REPORTED, readout_is_qualitative true and
  effect_direction NOT_REPORTED, so that "measured but only plotted" stays distinguishable from "never measured". No
  number was read off any figure anywhere in this bundle.

  Backbone chemistry is stated ("all PS") only for ISIS 404071, 404057 and 418026. For ISIS 401025, 405277 and 405278
  the Chemistry Motif column gives only "5-10-5 MOE gap" / "Uniform MOE" with no linkage chemistry, so
  backbone_chemistry is NOT_REPORTED for those three rather than assumed to be PS.

  No `modifications` rows for S32: "5-10-5 MOE gap" is a design shorthand, not a per-position publication with a legend,
  and the document never states 5-methyl-C status, which the modifications schema requires as a boolean. Modelling it
  from Isis house convention would be fabrication.

--- S61, US 7,538,211 (Archemix, ARC187) : the high-concentration negative ---
The scarce row type. Citrated human plasma titrated to 20 uM - by the patent's own framing "well in excess of projected
doses", and >10x the 1.5 uM steady-state plasma concentration the patent elsewhere targets clinically - gives NO CHANGE
in PT and only a slight aPTT elevation, for a PEGylated SELEX aptamer. Negatives at deliberately excessive concentration
on a modality distinct from gapmers and duplexes are what stop a model learning "oligonucleotide implies aPTT
prolongation". This is also the only source in the bundle that examines the oligo's INTERACTION with co-administered
heparin and protamine, which matters because the intended setting is cardiopulmonary bypass.

  STUDY-TYPE HAZARD (3 rows). EXAMPLE 6B is headed "In vivo Effects of ARC187 on Coagulation", but the example names no
  species, no subject, no route and no group size, and its readouts are ACT with the aptamer expressed as a plasma
  concentration. study_type and species are recorded NOT_REPORTED for those three rows rather than inferred from the
  heading. NOT_REPORTED is used here in preference to a schema enum value because the no-fabrication rule outranks enum
  tidiness; a reviewer should resolve it against FIG. 56 or the prosecution file.

  All nine ARC187 rows are qualitative. The only printed numbers in this section are the heparin-alone ACT controls
  (baseline ~150 s; ~500 s at 4 U/mL heparin; ~800 s at 5 U/mL heparin), which are recorded as control_value; the ACT
  values in the presence of ARC187 live only in the table of FIG. 55 and the graph of FIG. 56.

  Aptamer chemistry IS published per position with an explicit legend ("fC and fU=2'-fluoro nucleotides, and mG and
  mA=2'-OMe nucleotides and all other nucleotides are 2'-OH"), so ARC187 gets 38 modification rows. The trailing "-3T"
  residue printed in the structure is NOT covered by that legend and is therefore excluded from the modifications array
  rather than guessed at; the printed sequence retains it. Internucleotide linkage chemistry is stated nowhere for
  ARC187, so backbone_linkage_3p is NOT_REPORTED at all 38 positions.

--- S73, US 2014/0275214 A1 (Teva/OncoGenex, custirsen) : ranked last, and here is why ---
  THE CENTRAL PROBLEM. The triage note flagged that reduced aPTT prolongation is the INVENTION'S CLAIMED BENEFIT, and it
  is - the specification repeatedly recites that an up-titrated subject "is less likely to have aPTT prolongation than a
  corresponding human subject who is administered 640 mg ... 3 times in the 5 to 9 day period". But the document contains
  NO DATA supporting that claim. Example 1 is a narrative of already-completed Study TV1011-DDI-102 with no coagulation
  results; Examples 2 and 3, which administer the ascending 320/480/640 mg regimen, are written entirely in the
  present-tense protocol voice ("Up to 165 healthy adult men enroll in this study", "Objectives of the study are as
  follows") and report no results at all. The claimed aPTT benefit of up-titration is therefore PROPHETIC. Every
  extractable coagulation row in this document comes instead from the retrospective safety narrative under the heading
  "PTT Prolongation", and describes the FLAT 640 mg regimen and earlier studies - i.e. the comparator, not the invention.
  See refused_rows.

  The document contains no coagulation table and no numeric clotting time anywhere. All ten S73 rows are qualitative,
  counts (n_of_N with the denominator never printed), or upper-bounded.

  UPPER-BOUNDED VALUES. "no INR values above 1.5" and "INR did not exceed 1.5" are encoded as readout_value "<=1.5", the
  mirror image of S5's right-censored ">100". Do not read either as 1.5. For the OGX-011-01/02 row, effect_direction is
  NOT_REPORTED because the source bounds the maximum without saying whether INR moved at all; for the TV1011-DDI-102 row
  it is "increase" because the same sentence describes the value as the peak of a prolongation.

  "PTT" vs "aPTT": the safety narrative uses "PTT" while the document's own abbreviation list defines aPTT as activated
  partial thromboplastin time and the claims use "aPTT". Rows are recorded as readout_name aPTT with the mapping flagged
  in notes.

  Grades ("grade 1 increase in PTT", "grade 2 toxicity for PTT") are the source's own words, recorded verbatim in
  severity_stated_by_source. No severity grade was assigned by this extractor anywhere in this bundle.

--- ABSENCE vs SILENCE ---
effect_direction "no_change" is used ONLY where the source reports a measured null: S5 SEQ ID NOs 1/4/7 (explicitly
"negligible effect up to 100 μg/ml dose compared to a saline control experiment"), all six ARC187 no-effect rows, the
ISIS 401029 antidote-specificity control, and the three custirsen bleeding rows. It is never used for an endpoint the
source simply did not mention.

Reporting silences worth recording: none of the four documents reports fibrinogen, D-dimer, antithrombin, anti-Xa/anti-
IIa, individual coagulation-factor ACTIVITY assays (S32 measures Factor XI mRNA, not FXI activity), or thromboelastometry.
S5 measured only aPTT, not PT or TT. No row was written for any of those - their absence from this file is silence in the
sources, not a measured null.
